reservations.composition: Compose the shared native accounting tables and usage semantics; do not create a second conflicting native_accounting schema.

reservations.feature: Service-native subscription identity and legacy configuration retirement
reservations.composition: Activate only after real migrations 26 and 27. Back up first, retire legacy subscription configuration atomically without inferring services, preserve historical attribution and configured-empty restrictions, and refuse unsettled native ownership or cleanup.

Activate only after real migrations 26 through 28. Add private metadata-only account_oauth_attempts with durable once-only exchange claims, original actor/request/process and reserved-account identities, protected-reference and cleanup evidence. Never persist plaintext verifier, code, key or callback/authorization URL, cascade recovery evidence, or create placeholder predecessors.

Seed only the 26 added hosted preset identities once, preserving historical six-provider seed sets, saved Off state, deletions, UUIDs, custom providers and account associations. Migration 29 retains original OAuth ownership and must contain its real private attempt table before migration 30.

reservations.feature: General API OAuth credential profiles and token lifecycle
reservations.composition: Activate only after real migrations 26 through 30. Preserve original OpenRouter attempts and protected references. Store bounded private authentication profiles, token-generation references, once-only refresh claims and cleanup metadata; never persist access/refresh tokens, verifiers, device codes, browser URLs or user codes. Restore must preserve current exchange/refresh authority and unresolved cleanup.

policy: Reservations are not executable. Implement in order, or revise the reservation sequence on main before starting replacements; never fill a gap with a no-op migration. An unmerged version-25 database is an unknown layout and requires preservation and explicit recovery.
